analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and independently checked the replayed changes. FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift head lines 148-162 introduce state-based device-mask caching and enable chained speculative decoding. FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift:72-91 delegates scanning mask keys to the base constraint and uses -1 for matched states. Its visible allowedTokenIDs implementation (:55-67) agrees with that partition: stop progress does not affect scanning masks, and matched states return only answer-stop tokens. Existing wrapper transitions and state-exhaustion guards remain visible at :93-122. No concrete security regression is established by these changes alone.
FlintAnswerStopTests.swift head patch lines 197-209 tests shared-key mask equality and zero-budget rejection, but not sampler integration. EngineV2KVBackendPolicyTests.swift head patches at :31 and :258-269 add Flint automatic-paging and M5 concurrency expectations; tests do not establish actual production allocation behavior. No supplied changes demonstrate weakening T-041 account scoping, SSD encryption, retention or donation controls, nor authorization, attestation, transport encryption, billing or fan-helper authority.
Material remaining review under TB-007, T-007, T-010, T-028 and T-041: inspect the CBv2 sampler's cache namespace/lifetime, support for negative keys, device-mask memory bounds, and speculative invalidation against confirmed constraint state. Equal masks do not imply equal stop-progress transitions. Verify resource exhaustion cannot be bypassed by cached masks and that redraw/termination preserve stop filtering, cancellation and token accounting. Validate actual Flint paging/concurrency selection against KV budgets and request/cache isolation. These contracts are outside the supplied implementation evidence, not observed missing controls. Replay omits four previously reviewed units and contains only the native-constraint patch, limiting independent verification of surrounding behavior; further integration review is required before resolving these questions.
